findings.current: Unlike me, who merely nodded without much interest, Hyuk Mujin was so shocked that he nearly fell off his horse.
findings.defect: The draft changes an actual fall into a near fall. The later statement that Hyuk Mujin climbs back into the saddle confirms that he fell off.
findings.rationale: 말에서 떨어질 정도로, together with the subsequent 다시 안장에 오르며, establishes that Hyuk Mujin falls and then remounts.
findings.replacement: Unlike me, who merely nodded without much interest, Hyuk Mujin was so shocked that he fell off his horse.

findings.current:
“Listen to this old bastard calling me Young Hero Chul. Didn’t you call me a cow’s head earlier?”

“N-No, Great Hero Chul! I committed a grave discourtesy earlier!”

“Committed? You committed? ‘So’? You just called me a cow again, didn’t you?”
findings.defect: “Old bastard” intensifies 중늙은이, while the central joke is left opaque because the draft neither reproduces the repeated -소 sound nor explains that 소 also means “cow.”
findings.rationale: Chulwoo strips 저질렀소 down sound by sound until only 소 remains, then deliberately interprets it as “cow.” A brief footnote is warranted because that bilingual pun cannot be conveyed fully through natural English alone.
findings.replacement:
“Hah, listen to this old coot calling me Young Hero Chul. Didn’t you call me a cow’s head earlier?”

“N-No, Great Hero Chul! I committed a grave discourtesy, *so*!”

“Committed-*so*? *-so*? Cow? You just called me a cow again, didn’t you?”[^1]

[^1]: The formal Korean sentence ending *-so* (소) is pronounced the same as the Korean word for “cow.”
findings.source:
“허, 이 중늙은이가 철 소협 같은 소리 하네. 아까는 소대가리라면서?”

“아, 아니 철 대협! 아까는 내가 큰 결례를 저질렀소!”

“저질렀소? 질렀소? 렀소? 소? 지금 나보고 또 소라고 했지?”

findings.current:
“You’re welcome. Grandpa said that people who lack a firm will, like weak martial artists, need to be looked after constantly.”

“…”

For fuck’s sake. He was just doing mental-health care.
findings.defect: The draft turns 하수들 into an illustrative comparison rather than directly classifying Taekyung as one of the weak martial artists, weakening the accidental insult. “Doing mental-health care” is also unnatural English and blunts the punchline.
findings.rationale: The source directly describes low-level martial artists whose resolve is weak, revealing that Cheongpung’s apparent compliment was merely encouragement prescribed for someone he considers inferior.
findings.replacement:
“You’re welcome. Grandpa said weak martial artists without firm resolve need constant attention.”

“…”

Fuck me. It had just been a pep talk.
findings.source:
“아니에요. 할아버지께서 말씀하시길, 의지가 굳건하지 못한 하수들은 꾸준히 신경 써 주셔야 한다고 말씀하셨는걸요.”

“…….”

이런 시발, 멘탈 케어였네.

findings.current:
“What’s the name of the person who would be your grandfather?”

“Mae Jonghak.”
findings.defect: The question is awkwardly calqued, and Cheongpung’s deliberate explanation of the name’s component characters is omitted.
findings.rationale: Cheongpung does not merely state the name; he explicitly identifies its constituent name characters before repeating Mae Jonghak.
findings.replacement:
“May I ask your grandfather’s full name?”

“His surname is Mae, and his given name uses the characters Jong and Hak. Mae Jonghak.”
findings.source:

summary: One scene-action reversal and several meaningful omissions or register problems require correction.
